statement: How many real solutions does the equation $|x^2 - 6x| = 9$ have?

choices.misconception: I only used the case $x^2 - 6x = -9$, which gives just $x = 3$.
I only solved $x^2 - 6x = 9$ and forgot the case where the expression inside the absolute value equals $-9$.
I solved both cases but counted the repeated solution $x = 3$ of $(x - 3)^2 = 0$ twice.

hints: An absolute value equals $9$ when the expression inside equals $9$ or $-9$.
Solve $x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0$ and $x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0$ separately; the discriminant tells you how many real solutions each has.
The first has discriminant $36 + 36 = 72 > 0$, so it has two solutions; the second is $(x - 3)^2 = 0$, so it has one. Check that no solution is shared.

solutions.reliable: Case 1: $x^2 - 6x = 9$, or $x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0$. Its discriminant is $36 + 36 = 72 > 0$, so it has two real solutions, $x = 3 \pm 3\sqrt{2}$. Case 2: $x^2 - 6x = -9$, or $(x - 3)^2 = 0$, which has the single solution $x = 3$. Since $3$ is neither $3 + 3\sqrt{2}$ nor $3 - 3\sqrt{2}$, the three solutions are distinct, so the equation has $3$ real solutions.
solutions.elegant: Write $x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 9$. The equation says this equals $9$ or $-9$, so $(x - 3)^2 = 18$, with two solutions, or $(x - 3)^2 = 0$, with one solution: $3$ in all.
